title: Ziemian frame 1 (single-storey portal frame, fixed bases): elastic critical load ratio

source.work: C. W. Ziemian, R. D. Ziemian, Steel benchmark frames for structural analysis and validation studies: Finite element models and numerical simulation data, Data in Brief 39 (2021) 107564, doi:10.1016/j.dib.2021.107564, with the data set on Mendeley Data, doi:10.17632/39sjhchwtx.1

The model data of this frame are reproduced from the data set under that licence, converted to this project's input format (changes: 4 elements per member merged into one member, plane model embedded in 3D, 0.8 E entered as the modulus).

analysis: Frame 1 of the data set (single-storey portal frame, fixed bases), units kip and inch. Plane frame in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held (the data set's frames are 'fully braced out-of-plane'); in-plane bending about local z, so the data set's Izz is the section's Iz. Modulus 0.8 E = 23200 ksi (the data set's condition for all elastic analyses; its element table points to E = 29000 ksi, the published results correspond to 0.8 E - verified for this frame with the first-order displacements). No shear deformation. A straight line of the data set's elements is one member here, the loads at its interior nodes are point loads on the member. The data set's model is plane (no out-of-plane buckling of a member between joints); the engine's member is spatial, so Iy = 1000 Izz is entered for every section instead of the listed Iyy: no out-of-plane mode can precede the in-plane behaviour compared, and Iy does not enter the in-plane results. Linear buckling analysis on the PERFECT geometry with the loads as listed in the model file; target: the data set's elastic critical load ratio (MASTAN2 eigenvalue analysis, 4 elements per member with a polynomial geometric stiffness; 'lowest sway buckling mode'). The engine's members carry the exact stability functions.

targets.precisionNote: printed "7.857"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; number as displayed by the data set's spreadsheet (cell format 0.000); stored value 7.857008965387629
targets.sign: positive factor on the listed loads

quarantine.diagnosis: Cause: discretisation of the data set. Its ratio comes from an eigenvalue analysis with 4 elements per member and a polynomial geometric stiffness, which overestimates the critical load; the engine's members carry the exact stability functions. Evidence (verification/derive/ziemian_diagnosis.py): a plane-frame program written here with the data set's own elements (cubic elements, consistent geometric stiffness, axial forces of a linear analysis, perfect geometry, 0.8 E) gives 7.856995, the data set's stored value 7.857009 within 2e-06; the engine gives 7.856261, lower by 9.5e-05 of the value, which is more than half a unit of the third decimal the data set displays (7.857 against the engine's 7.856).
